articles.title: AMAJAZZON 2026: Amaro Freitas e Juliana Linhares no Theatro da Paz | G1
articles.standfirst: Festival acontece nos dias 21 e 22 de novembro, no Theatro da Paz, em Belém, com atrações brasileiras e internacionais. Ingressos já estão à venda a partir de R$ 90.
articles.summary: O Festival AMAJAZZON 2026 reúne Amaro Freitas, Juliana Linhares e Thomas Strønen no Theatro da Paz, em Belém, com ingressos à venda para os shows de novembro.
articles.body:
A cantora e compositora Juliana Linhares, o pianista pernambucano Amaro Freitas e o baterista norueguês Thomas Strønen — Foto: Divulgação

O pianista pernambucano Amaro Freitas, a cantora e compositora Juliana Linhares e o baterista norueguês Thomas Strønen estão entre as primeiras atrações confirmadas do Festival AMAJAZZON 2026, em Belém . A programação reúne nomes do jazz e da música brasileira, com destaque para Amaro Freitas, um dos principais representantes da música instrumental brasileira contemporânea, e Juliana Linhares, que chega ao festival com um álbum indicado ao Grammy Latino.

O festival também terá apresentações da Amazônia Jazz Band, com uma convidada especial, e de um ensemble universitário formado por músicos do Brasil e da Noruega. Os shows acontecem nos dias 21 e 22 de novembro, no Theatro da Paz, em Belém. Os ingressos já estão à venda online.

Em sua terceira edição, o AMAJAZZON reúne artistas da Amazônia, de outras regiões do Brasil e do exterior, com uma programação que aproxima o jazz e a música instrumental de diferentes tradições e linguagens musicais. O intercâmbio entre músicos brasileiros e internacionais é uma das propostas do festival desde sua criação.

“O intercâmbio cultural e musical no AMAJAZZON é vital para enriquecer o cenário artístico tanto dos músicos locais quanto dos visitantes internacionais. Ao compartilharem palcos, esses artistas trocam experiências, técnicas e perspectivas”, afirmou Anabela Cunha, da Connecting Dots, organizadora do festival.

Um dos nomes de maior projeção internacional do jazz brasileiro contemporâneo, Amaro Freitas desenvolveu uma linguagem própria ao aproximar a improvisação do jazz de ritmos como frevo, maracatu e baião. Sua pesquisa também estabelece uma conexão direta com a Amazônia, que inspirou o álbum Y'Y (2024), criado a partir de experiências na região e do contato com indígenas Sateré-Mawé. O trabalho reúne participações de músicos internacionais como Shabaka, Brandee Younger e Jeff Parker.

Da Noruega, Thomas Strønen traz ao festival sua pesquisa em improvisação e experimentação sonora. Baterista e compositor com trajetória na cena europeia do jazz contemporâneo, o músico explora diferentes possibilidades expressivas da percussão, construindo diálogos entre ritmo, silêncio e texturas musicais.

Outra atração confirmada é Juliana Linhares, cantora, compositora e atriz potiguar que apresenta o espetáculo Até Cansar o Cansaço, inspirado em seu segundo álbum solo, indicado ao Grammy Latino na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música de Raízes em Língua Portuguesa. Com participações de Ney Matogrosso, Anastácia e Agnes Nunes, o disco transforma reflexões sobre o esgotamento contemporâneo em canções que atravessam a tradição nordestina, a experimentação e a força cênica da artista. No palco, Juliana combina música, teatro e movimento, em um repertório que também inclui sucessos como “Balanceiro” e “Bombinha”.

A presença amazônica na programação ganha destaque com a Amazônia Jazz Band, formação paraense que aproxima o repertório do jazz de referências musicais regionais e se apresenta com uma convidada especial. O festival também promove um encontro entre músicos universitários do Brasil e da Noruega, ampliando o intercâmbio internacional que integra a identidade do AMAJAZZON.

“A expectativa do festival é criar um ambiente de aprendizado mútuo e inspiração, além de abrir novos caminhos para colaborações futuras e fortalecer a presença global da música da Amazônia”, destaca Anabela Cunha.

Onde: Theatro da Paz, Avenida da Paz, Praça da República, s/n, Campina, Belém (PA).

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence’s Husband Begged Her to ‘Get a Hotel Room’ After Testing a Haircare Product That Made Her Smell Like Fish
articles.summary: The Oscar winner’s brand, Mes, launched on Oct. 27 with three products
articles.body:
Jennifer Lawrence told The Cut that she started to smell like fish while testing a hair mask for her new brand, Mes

The actress recalled her husband, Cooke Moroney, asking her to "get a hotel room" if she didn't wash it out

The Oscar winner's brand launched on Oct. 27 with three products

Jennifer Lawrence really committed to testing products for her new haircare brand, Mes.

The actress, 36, opened up about the venture in an interview with The Cut for its October 2026 cover, admitting that an unscented version of Mes' hair mask made her hair smell like fish when she left it on for four days.

"My husband was like, 'If you don't wash your hair, you have to get a hotel room," she recalled to the outlet.

Lawrence married art gallery director Cooke Maroney in 2019. The couple welcomed their first child , son Cy , in 2022, and in April 2025, sources confirmed to PEOPLE the arrival of the pair's second child , a son whose name hasn't been revealed to the public.

The Oscar winner's hair brand launched on Tuesday, Oct. 27, with three products: a repair mask, a restyling serum and a volumizing mist.

She explained to The Cut why the business move made sense for her career, saying, "There is an undeniable energetic thing that happens when you're creating things, whether it's a movie or a product. I got that same electric buzz I get from building a character. It's like, Well, I have to follow this because it's the same animal. "

However, Lawrence said she's still not sure how to talk about the brand. "I have to pretend I've made the greatest thing on earth," she shared. "Otherwise it gets too scary. It's a form of forced manifestation."

In the interview, the actress also shared her aspiration to be a "sexy mom," also touching on her plans to get a facelift in the future.

"I want to be a sexy mom," she said. "At drop-off, I want to look like a woman that has her s--t together even when I've just woken up and don't have my s--t together."

During a press conference at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2025, Lawrence opened up about how becoming a parent has affected her career.

"Having children changes everything. It changes your whole life. It's brutal and incredible," she said. "Not only do they go into every decision of if I'm working, where I'm working, when I'm working — they've taught me ... and they've opened up the world to me."

articles.title: Erin Foster, Tovah Feldshuh respond after 'Nobody Wants This' star Adam Brody calls to 'free Palestine'
articles.summary: The comments, made in a September interview with GQ, have since drawn backlash from some of Brody's collaborators on the show.
articles.body:
Adam Brody, the star of Nobody Wants This, expressed his support for the Palestinian people in a recent interview, stating that he believes the conflict in Gaza is a genocide. Brody plays a rabbi who explores an interfaith relationship in the hit Netflix series, which premiered in 2024.

The comments, made in a September interview with GQ , have since drawn criticism from some of Brody's collaborators on the show, including creator Erin Foster and actor Tovah Feldshuh, who plays Brody's onscreen mom.

In the GQ interview, Brody opened up about his history of activism and volunteer work with Swing Left , a political organization dedicated to educating voters in swing districts. When asked whether Hollywood had become more conservative, the actor said yes, then acknowledged that some of his peers' beliefs had surprised him.

"I wasn't looking under the hood too much, but you considered everyone to be like-minded," Brody said. "Between COVID, a second Trump term, Israel-Gaza, it's really brought out some different beliefs that I was ignorant to, and then disheartened by."

Brody went on to admit that while he's "spoken a lot" about the war between Israel and Hamas privately, he hasn't said much publicly. When asked whether he wanted to speak about it during the interview, Brody voiced his support for "a free Palestine," while also referring to the conflict in Gaza as genocide.

"Put me down as thinking it's a genocide," he said. "Put me down as wanting a free Palestine. It's awful that it's taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it's reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago. I'm hopeful that another administration can really do some good and correct some of these policies that are helping that situation be as awful as it is."

Erin Foster appeared on the Oct. 27 episode of Amanda Hirsch's Not Skinny but Not Fat podcast , during which she addressed Brody's stance.

"It's complicated," Foster said. "I think our work environment, our set is very similar to dinner tables around the world, where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing. And, you know, while I love Adam, I also disagree with him, and that's OK."

Nobody Wants This is based on Foster's own experience of converting to Judaism before marrying her husband, Simon Tikhman, in 2019. While speaking to Hirsch, Foster voiced support for the show's "Jewish fans," adding, "I see you and I hear you and I understand how you feel."

"The show has always been and always will be a love letter to Judaism. That is why I made this show," she continued. "It's because of how beautiful of an experience I've had becoming Jewish and being a Jewish person. And sitting here right now, at this time in the world where there is almost zero positive representation of Jewish people, I think it's so important to have that."

In an interview with the New York Post published on Oct. 25, the Nobody Wants This star condemned celebrities who refer to the Israel-Hamas conflict as genocide. Tovah Feldshuh described the discourse as having a "horseshoe effect," where "socialism and antisemitism are trying to meet."

"To accuse the Jewish people of genocide is wild," she said. "It's right out of Hitler's playbook. You take the victim and you make the victim the perpetrator."

Feldshuh told the New York Post that such comments made by Jewish people themselves "makes a difference to the [Jewish] community."

"I believe that the perseverance of the existence of the state of Israel is crucial to the well-being of the democratic world and of the free world," she continued. "Of course, Israel needs the United States, [but] the United States needs Israel, believe you me."

Former rabbi consultant criticizes Brody

Steve Leder, who served as a rabbi consultant for Brody during Season 1 of Nobody Wants This , also criticized the actor's comments.

"Your pronouncement the other day about a genocide in Gaza was truly shocking," Leder said in an Instagram video posted on Sept. 29. "There is no genocide in Gaza."

images.caption: Erin Foster, Adam Brody and Tovah Feldshuh. (Photo illustration: Yahoo News; photos: JC Olivera/WireImage via Getty Images, Christopher Polk/Deadline via Getty Images, Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images)
Foster and Brody in 2024. (Charley Gallay/Getty Images for Netflix)

articles.title: Danny Masterson Fails To Get Double Rape Conviction Overturned; No Bias Against Scientology, Appeals Court Rules
articles.summary: Three years after being convicted of raping two women, Danny Masterson on Tuesday saw his appeal hopes disappear and allegations that Scientology was unfairl...
articles.body:
Three years after being convicted of raping two women, Danny Masterson on Tuesday saw his appeal hopes disappear and allegations that Scientology was unfairly dragged into his two trials rejected — at least for now.

"The judgment is affirmed," a trio of judges from the Second Appellate District ruled today on Masterson's challenge against L.A. Superior Court Judge Charlaine Olmedo's conduct during the two trials and the subsequent 30-year sentence he received.

"The trial court permitted evidence that the victims had a pending civil action for damages against defendant, Scientology, and Miscavige, alleging claims of harassment and stalking," the 89-page ruling from the appeals panel said on the claims by the That 70s Show star and his faith that Olmedo inappropriately allowed material about the Church, Masterson and his victims' roles in Scientology, its inner workings and leader David Miscavige into the 2022 and 2023 cases. "The trial court also permitted evidence of the settlement agreement between defendant and J.B. and the amount paid to J.B. pursuant to that settlement."

"Admission of Scientology evidence did not violate the First Amendment and was not an abuse of the trial court's discretion," the panel determined, undercutting one of Masterson's main thrusts to get his 30-year sentence dismissed or a new trial. The three judges added: "The jury in this case was not asked to determine the truth or falsity of Scientology doctrine or beliefs. Admission of Scientology evidence for those purposes did not contravene the First Amendment."

With today's ruling, Masterson remains ineligible for parole until 2042.

Representatives of the Church of Scientology did not respond to Deadline's request for comment on today's ruling. However, Masterson's attorneys Cliff Gardner and Eric Multhaup tell Deadline they are going to try to take the matter to the California Supreme Court. Additionally, they intend "to pursue habeas corpus relief based on substantial exculpatory evidence that was never presented to the jury."

Masterson was arrested in 2020 over the alleged assaults that occurred between 2001 and 2003 in his Hollywood Hills house. He had been out on a bail of $3 million until May 31, 2023, when the guilty verdict in his second trial on two of three counts of sexual assault was handed down.

Both of the women Masterson was convicted of raping in were members of Scientology at the time of the assaults.

In depositions and testimony, both women, known as J.B. and N.T. during the trial, said they were told by officials at Scientology not to report the incidents to the police or face expulsion from the Church and its entire community — including their families. The appeal petition of late 2025 says that trial defense lawyer Phillip Cohen should have stared down the judge and the DA's office. Masterson wanted a representative of Scientology to take the stand to lay out its internal processes and dispute the expulsion claims. As the appeals filing of November 2025 made clear, if that testimony had happened, Masterson believed the second trial could have ended differently.

Masterson, a onetime prominent Scientology member. was facing up to 45 years behind bars if found guilty on all three rape counts in the first trial and the subsequent retrial involving J.B. and N.T. After being given his sentence by Olmedo on September 7, 2023 , Masterson was immediately taken into custody, and later denied bail as a "flight risk."

Sweeping up other objections by Masterson involving the LAPD, admitted evidence, pretrial procedures and more, the appeals court Tuesday concluded: "We reject defendant's contention that the cumulative effect of the claimed errors identified in his appeal deprived him of due process of law and a fair trial. Because we have found none of the claimed errors to constitute individual errors, they cannot as a group constitute cumulative error."

Masterson was incarcerated in California's high-security Corcoran State Prison before being moved in early 2024 due to threats. He is currently serving time at the California's Men's Colony in San Luis Obispo, which houses around 3,4000 inmates and is both a medium- and minimum-security facility.

articles.title: Los regalos de Irene Montero y Gabriel Rufián a David Broncano: "Unas rodilleras, que dicen que las uso mucho"
articles.standfirst: La eurodiputada de Podemos lanza un dardo a Abascal en 'La Revuelta'
articles.summary: La eurodiputada de Podemos lanza un dardo a Abascal en 'La Revuelta'
articles.body: Gabriel Rufián, portavoz de ERC en el Congreso de los Diputados, e Irene Montero, eurodiputada y candidata de Podemos, ha compartido la noche con David Broncano en 'La Revuelta'. Ambos le han traído regalos al presentador. El portavoz de ERC ha aparecido en el plató con una caja. Gabriel Rufián le ha mostrado a Broncano una botella de aceite de Jaén y un maletín oficial del Congreso: "Por si eres diputado del PSOE". Para Abascal, líder de Vox, un despertador: "Nunca se le ha visto a las 9:00, la España que madruga, los cojo***". En el caso de que venga Feijóo, del Partido Popular, el dirigente catalán ha traído una fotografía enmarcada de Pablo Casado, ex del PP. Irene Montero, por su parte, le ha regalado unas rodilleras para Abascal, que tiene las puertas abiertas para acudir a 'La Revuelta': "Dicen muchas veces que las uso mucho, pero los que están arrodillados ante Trump y Netanyahu son ellos". David Broncano, por su parte, le ha dado la razón a la dirigente de Podemos, recordando que este comentario se le ha trasladado en varias ocasiones a Irene Montero. La madrileña también ha regalado una correa para el muñeco que un perro que trajo el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, en su última visita al programa. "Le he traído una correa muy mona porque si tú quieres que baje el precio de los alquileres, necesitas ponerle la correa al perro que, si no, se nos va para la derecha", ha recalcado.

articles.title: 'Rolling Stone' releases list of 200 greatest 21st century rock songs and it's as awful as you'd imagine
articles.summary: "Rolling Stone" ranked "Maps" by the Yeah Yeah Yeah's as the greatest 21st century rock song, snubbing Blink-182 and System of a Down in the process.
articles.body: Anyone of a certain age who is even tangentially familiar with rock music knows that, for a time, "Rolling Stone" magazine was almost the foremost expert on all things involving the genre. In recent decades, however, the once-proud music mag has devolved into hipster drivel, and nowhere is that more evident than in their ranking lists. From their infamous "250 Greatest Guitarists of All-Time" (in which they ranked Joni Mitchell and someone named Sister Rosetta Tharpe over Tony Iommi and Eric Clapton) to the perplexing "500 Greatest Albums of All-Time," the fine folks over at "Rolling Stone" have released some stinkers, opting to let their contrarian opinions and eye-rollingly leftist leanings color their rankings. RANKING THE TEN BEST BILLY JOEL SONGS OF ALL TIME IN HONOR OF THE PIANO MAN'S 77TH BIRTHDAY "Greatest" is a subjective term, especially when it comes to music, but when large swathes of the entire internet take exception to your rankings, you might have to reevaluate some things. On that note, it looks like "Rolling Stone" has released yet another God-awful list, this time in the form of "The 200 Greatest Rock Songs of The 21st Century So Far." I'll be frank with you, I don't really hold a lot of 21st century rock in high regard. I'm a child of the '90s, but my musical tastes predate someone of my birth year by a good two decades, consisting mainly of rock and metal acts from the 1970s, '80s, and '90s. SIX ROCK BANDS WHO GOT BETTER AFTER REPLACING KEY MEMBERS Even then, I can admit that there is plenty of great rock to be found on this side of the year 2000, but "Rolling Stone's" list eschews most of that to try and cobble together this eclectic ranking to boost their street cred with all the gender-fluid dorks from Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn (aka, the only people still reading "Rolling Stone"). Let's start at the top and see what they selected as the "greatest" rock song of the 21st century. "Maps" by the Yeah Yeah Yeah's. Are we serious here? If your response is, "Who the hell are the Yeah Yeah Yeahs?" congrats, you’re not alone. The only reason I know this song, unfortunately, is because I used to watch Fuse TV in the early 2000s and this boring, monotonous song and accompanying music video would interrupt all the fun pop-punk acts I actually wanted to see, but I digress. This song taking the top spot is just a harbinger of things to come, so sit back as I regale you with some of the more egregious placements and omissions on this list. For starters, I think "Rolling Stone" needs to reevaluate what the word "rock" means, because there are some musical acts dotting the upper spots of this ranking that probably shouldn't even be on here at all. Would any of you make a rock playlist and add Lana Del Rey, Jay-Z, MGMT, Taylor Swift, and/or Lady Gaga to it? If you answered "yes," then congratulations! You're either certifiably insane or you write for "Rolling Stone" (and those two things aren't exactly mutually exclusive). Some of the songs that got shafted by whoever wrote this list are staggering. CHAD GILBERT, NEW FOUND GLORY FOUNDING MEMBER AND LEAD GUITARIST, DEAD AT 45 "The Middle" by Jimmy Eat World is in the top-25, and deservedly so, but one of the pop-punk anthems of the early aughts is ranked lower than such "classics" as Geese's "Getting Killed," Mitski's "Your Best American Girl," and "Night Shift" by Lucy Dacus. If I gathered 100 random people off the street and asked them if they knew any of those three songs, I bet the hit rate would be about 3%. What does "Rolling Stone" mean when they say "greatest?" Because if you ask me, how iconic a song is in the cultural zeitgeist as well as its crossover appeal and impact on pop culture should be taken into account. I guess you really can't overstate just how impactful Mitski was on the rock scene in the early 2020s, can you? Some more head-scratchers include Queens of the Stone Age's "No One Knows" coming in at a robust 36, three spots behind Slater-Kinney's "Entertain." Man, when I think of rock, I would definitely pick Slater-Kinney over one of the best alternative acts of the 2000s! System of a Down's "Chop Suey" also misses the top-25 entirely, as does Panic! At The Disco's "I Write Sins Not Tragedies." Blink-182 is almost completely unrepresented on this list, and their highest-ranked entry, "Rock Show," failed to even crack the top-50. I can't think of five rock bands from the 21st century who had more of an impact on music than Blink-182, yet here we are. Others were similarly shafted (Velvet Revolver, Sum 41), but the list did get a few right. The Strokes' "Last Nite" was included in the top-10 (although their 2003 classic "Reptilia" was still too low for my liking) and the song that just missed the top spot was none other than "Seven Nation Army" by White Stripes, a very deserving song to include in the top-five. You can read the entire list for yourself, but suffice to say if you're a fan of traditional rock music — or things that make sense in general — you're probably going to need to take some blood pressure medication ahead of time. Then again, as my colleague and fellow metal-head Matt Reigle pointed out, "Rolling Stone" is likely doing this just to get a rise out of old heads like us. "What the f—? '99 Problems' is in the top-ten?" Yes, "Rolling Stone," you've done your job. I fell for your rage bait hook, line and sinker. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Just know that the rock community at large is laughing at you, not with you.

articles.title: Gaza’s women filmmakers turn pain into cinema as new academy launches
articles.summary: Gaza film festival highlights women’s resilience through stories of war, loss and survival.
articles.body:
Al-Bureij, Gaza Strip – A Sack of Flour, an 11-minute documentary by the emerging filmmaker Mona Abu Qass, draws on her personal experience to examine Israel’s use of starvation against Palestinians in Gaza during Israel’s genocidal war on the enclave.

The film is one of five documentaries by Palestinian women screened Monday at the opening of the second Gaza International Women’s Film Festival, which also marked the official launch of the Gaza Cinema Academy.

The event took place at the site of the al-Nakheel Hall in al-Bureij, central Gaza, under the slogan “Women Creating Life from Death”. The hall is destroyed, like the majority of buildings in Gaza, after three years of Israel’s war, which has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians.

The film captures Palestinians’ struggle to find food in Gaza, the dangers at aid distribution points and the lives lost while trying to obtain flour.

Through Abu Qass’s own experiences, A Sack of Flour explores how the trauma of hunger continues to affect families even after food becomes available again.

Those experiences have renewed relevance as Israeli restrictions on goods entering Gaza and cuts to food assistance have caused shortages and fears of a return to famine.

“The idea for the film stems from a personal experience and a true story,” Abu Qass told Al Jazeera. “It documents daily life in Gaza, weighed down by bombardment, destruction, siege, hunger, and loss.”

“I want to capture details that reveal suffering and people’s determination to hold on to their life,” she added. “I seek to show reality as people experience it and help viewers understand what the war has done to their relationships, dreams, and hopes.”

Another film, Beyond Silence, by emerging filmmaker and journalist Raghda al-Buhaisi, explores wartime struggles in Gaza for people with disabilities through the story of a deaf artist who never learned to read, write or communicate through sign language. His art studio in southern Gaza’s Rafah was destroyed by Israel, and his parents and several family members were killed.

After being displaced to Deir el-Balah in central Gaza, another family took him in and set up a modest studio by the roadside. His paintings reflect loss and displacement, expressing what words cannot through colour and line.

“I want to highlight the additional challenges people with disabilities face during war, including displacement, family loss, and the destruction of livelihoods,” al-Buhaisi told Al Jazeera. “Art can cross barriers of language and silence, turning an individual experience of pain into a visual message that conveys Gaza’s suffering to the world.”

Alongside those films were three others by emerging Palestinian women filmmakers – Soso: The Lifeline, Remnants of Light, and Dandana. The films document life in Gaza and the suffering brought by war.

Soso: The Lifeline follows an orphaned child and his donkey, who help people survive in Gaza. Remnants of Light follows a filmmaker struggling with the loss of her family and home, while Dandana tells the story of a mother whose eight children were killed, and who turns to Palestinian songs with her surviving family to cope with her grief.

The five documentaries were produced through a filmmaking diploma programme that began in March and brought together 25 young Palestinian women.

Festival director Ezzedine Shallah said the films draw on experiences women and girls lived through during the war, offering visual testimony to daily life and giving women space to tell their stories in their own voices.

“Though their subjects differ, the films turn individual pain into broader human stories, revealing war’s psychological and social scars,” he told Al Jazeera. “They preserve stories that might otherwise never reach the screen, transforming suffering into cinematic testimony and bringing Gaza’s stories to audiences beyond its borders.”

The festival, which runs until October 31, features 73 films from 24 countries and offers a broader platform for filmmakers from Gaza and beyond.

But even with events like the festival, filmmaking in Gaza comes with formidable challenges. The destruction of cultural institutions, scarce equipment, limited funding, power and internet outages, and the pressures of war and displacement have severely restricted opportunities for film production. Women filmmakers also struggle to access training, production opportunities and international festivals.

Filmmaker Rima Mahmoud, a co-founder of the festival, said that war and the Israeli siege on Gaza – which predates 2023 – have hindered young women’s filmmaking, pushing some to use simple methods, self-fund projects and document Gaza’s reality even with the difficulties.

“Despite limited resources, these films deserve international exposure,” Mahmoud said. “Their makers need technical and financial support, translation, and partnerships with festivals and platforms.”

Palestinian filmmaker Mai Masri, based in Lebanon and another co-founder of the festival, said the films help young women tell their own stories, resist erasure and preserve collective memory, while building skills and accessing work in Gaza or through digital platforms.

The academy has also developed a filmmaking diploma in cooperation with al-Quds Open University and accredited by the Palestinian Ministry of Education.

Masri said that the academy is also now trying to help directors reach international festivals.

“We are seeking agreements with distributors to screen these films in educational and cultural institutions outside Palestine, and through international platforms and festivals focused on women’s and human rights,” she said.

“This would bring the voices of Palestinian women to a global audience, shed light on their human experiences and artistic creativity, strengthen the presence of Palestinian cinema internationally, and open new horizons for young female directors to reach global screening platforms and film festivals,” Masri added.

articles.title: Parque Permanente de Exposições Ribeirão Preto terá arena de R$ 135 mi | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudos preveem também praça de acesso gratuito e obras no recinto de festivais e feiras. Prefeitura pretende publicar edital até o fim de 2026, mas projeto depende da Câmara.
articles.summary: A concessão do Parque Permanente de Exposições de Ribeirão Preto prevê arena multiuso e área de lazer com investimento de R$ 135 milhões e obras previstas até 2028.
articles.body:
O Parque Permanente de Exposições de Ribeirão Preto (SP) poderá ganhar uma arena multiuso coberta para shows e eventos, uma praça de convivência com áreas de lazer e nova infraestrutura para receber festivais e feiras. Os estudos da concessão preveem R$ 134,8 milhões em obras iniciais, pagas pela empresa que vencer a licitação e administrar o espaço por 35 anos.

Os estudos foram apresentados pelo Consórcio Arena Ribeirão e analisados por uma comissão da Prefeitura. Em 29 de setembro, a comissão recomendou aproveitar o material na continuidade do processo, mas ressalvou que isso não significa adotar automaticamente valores, projetos e regras. A Prefeitura pode ajustá-los.

O projeto ainda depende de aprovação da Câmara Municipal e de licitação. Segundo o secretário municipal de Administração, João Rafael Mião, a Prefeitura pretende publicar o edital até o fim de 2026 e trabalha com a previsão de concluir as obras em 2028.

"A ideia mesmo é que seja feita a concessão para uma requalificação do espaço, porque Ribeirão Preto merece um espaço bem construído, um espaço adequado, bonito e agradável para o município usufruir", afirmou Mião.

Projeto arquitetônico do novo Parque Permanente de Exposições em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Prefeitura de Ribeirão Preto

A principal novidade é uma arena multiuso coberta, planejada para shows, congressos, feiras, apresentações culturais e eventos esportivos.

O modelo de contrato exige capacidade mínima de 10 mil pessoas. No projeto de referência dos estudos, a pista comportaria 15.075 pessoas, além de 138 camarotes. A arena teria áreas de alimentação, espaços de apoio aos artistas e um palco reversível, que poderia ser usado tanto dentro da estrutura quanto em eventos na área aberta do parque.

O projeto prevê ainda uma praça externa de 14,6 mil metros quadrados, com arborização, quiosques, espaços gastronômicos, parque infantil, academia ao ar livre e área para animais de estimação.

O atual recinto de exposições, usado em eventos como o Ribeirão Rodeo Music e o Festival João Rock, deverá receber melhorias nas redes de energia elétrica, água e esgoto, além de iluminação, pavimentação, drenagem, acessibilidade e acessos. A proposta inclui também a reorganização dos estacionamentos e das áreas de montagem e operação dos eventos.

Projeto preve revitalização e concessão do Parque Permanente de Exposições em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Prefeitura de Ribeirão Preto

O que fica para a população e para a Prefeitura

Pelo modelo apresentado, a praça externa deve ficar aberta gratuitamente todos os dias, das 8h às 18h. A regra não garante acesso gratuito irrestrito à arena e às demais áreas do complexo.

Os estudos preveem que a Prefeitura possa usar, sem pagar pelo espaço, uma data por ano na arena e três no parque de exposições. Os custos dos eventos nessas datas ficariam com o município.

A empresa vencedora também pagaria à Prefeitura uma outorga fixa, valor pago pelo direito de explorar o espaço. O mínimo previsto é de R$ 1.049.168,54. Há ainda uma outorga variável, de até 3% da receita líquida anual. Ao fim dos 35 anos, o parque volta para o município.

O estudo econômico-financeiro divide os R$ 134,8 milhões previstos inicialmente em três partes:

R$ 101,3 milhões: construção da arena multiuso;

R$ 24 milhões: reforma e modernização do parque de exposições;

R$ 9,5 milhões: implantação da praça externa.

Além desse valor, os estudos estimam outros R$ 44,6 milhões em melhorias e substituição de equipamentos ao longo dos 35 anos, o que leva o total a R$ 179,4 milhões.

"Esse investimento é aplicado pela empresa que for a vencedora da concessão", explicou o secretário.

Em contrapartida, a concessionária poderá explorar o complexo comercialmente, com eventos, locação de espaços, estacionamento, alimentação e outras atividades previstas no contrato.

Ainda não há data. O projeto está na fase de preparação da concessão. Depois de receber os estudos do consórcio, a Prefeitura fez uma audiência pública em 16 de outubro para discutir a proposta.

Segundo Mião, as sugestões recebidas passam por análise antes de o processo seguir para a Procuradoria do Município. Depois, a Prefeitura pretende enviar à Câmara um projeto de lei que autorize a concessão. Com a aprovação dos vereadores, poderá abrir a licitação para escolher a empresa que fará as obras e administrará o espaço.

"A ideia nossa é que a gente consiga publicar esse edital ainda em 2026", afirmou.

A Prefeitura prevê entregar o complexo em 2028. Os estudos, porém, estimam cerca de dois anos entre o projeto e a obra da arena, contados a partir da ordem de início do contrato. Por isso, o cronograma depende da aprovação na Câmara, da licitação e da contratação da concessionária.

Projeto arquitetônico do novo Parque Permanente de Exposições, em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Prefeitura de Ribeirão Preto

articles.title: Direita volta a usar funk e é acusada de hipocrisia | G1
articles.standfirst: Políticos conservadores que no passado associaram festas em favelas à 'narcocultura' agora embalam comemorações e vídeos eleitorais ao som do ritmo.
articles.summary: Políticos conservadores que no passado associaram festas em favelas à 'narcocultura' agora embalam comemorações e vídeos eleitorais ao som do ritmo.
articles.body:
Funk de camapnha do Flávio viralizou entre os jovens — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Durante a campanha eleitoral de 2026, candidatos da direita passaram a usar jingles de funk para alcançar o público jovem e viralizar nas redes sociais. A estratégia, no entanto, não conseguiu atrair nomes do gênero e foi alvo de críticas por uma possível hipocrisia .

Nomes como Eduarda Campopiano (PL), Nikolas Ferreira (PL), Lucas Pavanato (PL) e Flávio Bolsonaro fizeram diversos atos públicos tendo o funk como trilha.

Das 50 músicas mais ouvidas no país no domingo (25) de segundo turno, segundo o Spotify, seis eram canções de apoio ao candidato do PL à presidência ou com críticas a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Os funks de direita viraram música-tema das campanhas e invadiram as caixas de som dos apoiadores antes e durante a apuração.

Mas uma proximidade de candidatos de direita com o gênero, como se deu principalmente nas eleições de 2024, não rolou em 2026.

O funk ganhou espaço e foi hit entre os jovens que apoiam o candidato do PL . Músicas populares tiveram suas letras adaptadas com mensagens de apoio ao candidato e críticas ao PT.

Uma das versões que mais ganharam destaque traz o refrão "Quem ficar parado é petista disfarçado", usado para incentivar o público a dançar e pular durante as manifestações.

O funk embalou atos de campanha de Flávio em diferentes cidades. Em Vitória (ES), o candidato dançou ao som do funk em cima de um trio elétrico, acompanhado de aliados como o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL).

O uso do gênero conflita com discursos e posições de políticos de direita, que apontam uma suposta relação do ritmo com aquilo que classificam como uma narcocultura - conjunto de símbolos, valores e estéticas construídos em torno do tráfico de drogas..

Quando a hipocrisia no discurso é apontada, esses mesmos políticos dizem que suas críticas não são ao gênero em si, mas às letras de algumas canções e às festas de rua em favelas.

Em São Paulo, por exemplo, Lucas Pavanato celebrou sua eleição à Câmara dos Deputados ao som de funk.

Como vereador paulistano, ele foi relator da CPI dos Pancadões na Câmara, que investigava "bailes clandestinos e a perturbação do sossego público".

O vereador Rubinho Nunes (União Brasil) bateu boca com o chamado 'Chavoso da USP' durante a CPI dos Pancadões, — Foto: Douglas Ferreira/Rede Câmara SP

No seu relatório final, apontou que os pancadões funcionam como "espaços de difusão e normalização da chamada narcocultura".

Entre os interrogados na CPI estavam MC Ryan SP e MC Dricka, dois dos principais nomes do gênero. Eles reclamaram da forma como o funk, como gênero musical e expressão cultural, foi tratado pela comissão.

Desde que ganhou evidência a partir dos anos 2010, o funk de São Paulo se manteve apolítico.

O primeiro passo de aproximação com a política institucional se deu quando Rodrigo Oliveira, fundador da GR6, principal produtora do gênero no país, concorreu a vereador por São Paulo. Ele recebeu pouco mais de oito mil votos e acabou não eleito.

Nas eleições de 2018 e 2022, a polarização presidencial dividiu os MCs. Em 2022, os principais nomes do gênero, entre MCs e empresários como Konrad Dantas, o Kondzilla, fizeram uma reunião com Lula e declararam voto no petista.

No entanto, dois anos depois, boa parte dos funkeiros mudou de lado. Enquanto alguns apoiaram Ricardo Nunes (com direito a reunião do candidato na GR6), nomes grandes como o próprio MC Ryan SP e Henrique Alexandre Barros Viana, conhecido como "Rato", dono da produtora de funk Love Funk, apoiaram Pablo Marçal.

(Da dir. p/ esq.): Henrique Viana ao lado de Pablo Marçal; Ricardo Nunes na GR6 — Foto: Reprodução

O candidato outsider viu no funk uma oportunidade de se comunicar com os mais jovens e fortalecer ainda mais sua presença nas redes sociais. A associação de figuras importantes do gênero a um político declaradamente de direita gerou forte reação de outros MCs e de parte do público.

Essa rejeição fez com que em 2026 muitos funkeiros apoiassem Lula, caso dos MCs Hariel, Tuto, PH e IG, ou se mantivessem neutros, o que não impediu o uso do gênero pelas campanhas de direita.

Do lado dos políticos de direita, a justificativa para o uso do gênero passa como um direito à liberdade criativa.

Pavanato, por exemplo, afirmou que "o problema com o funk, por óbvio, é a letra, não o ritmo".

Outras figuras ligadas à direita, como Renan Santos, que também já ligou o funk a uma cultura "narcoterrorista", criticaram a utilização do gênero em jingles de candidatos conservadores.

"As pessoas viam esses vídeos, viam essas músicas, e não queriam isso para elas. As pessoas viam o Pavanato dançando e achavam mais repugnante que um petista clássico. Soa muito escroto."

articles.title: Como 2026 se tornou o ano em que ‘show de estádio’ virou algo comum no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Matemática das produtoras favorece eventos únicos em estádios quase vazios em vez de várias datas em casas menores. Novas arenas tentam equilibrar mercado até 2028.
articles.summary: Matemática das produtoras favorece eventos únicos em estádios quase vazios em vez de várias datas em casas menores. Novas arenas tentam equilibrar mercado até 2028.
articles.body:
Jorge Ben Jor se apresenta no Nubank Parque, no dia 17 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação/Lais Moss

A partir de 2023, com o pós-pandemia, o Brasil viu explodir um mercado que antes funcionava a passos lentos: o de shows em estádios. Em 2026, este cenário se consolidou . Show em estádio, que antes era um acontecimento, virou algo comum.

Tendo São Paulo como epicentro deste fenômeno, o país assumiu o posto de principal protagonista do continente, com o Nubank Parque, estádio do Palmeiras, como maior estrela. Hoje, está no top 10 de estádios que mais vendem ingressos de shows no mundo .

A expectativa da WTorre, responsável pelo estádio, é que o espaço receba cerca de 50 shows até o fim de 2026.

Esse movimento é explicado por fatores, sociais e monetários, mas também criou uma ilusão de demanda generalizada: nem todo mundo está pronto para lotar um estádio .

Em novembro de 2023, a estrela do pop Taylor Swift realizou seis shows no Brasil: três no Engenhão, no Rio de Janeiro, e três no hoje Nubank Parque.

A série de seis apresentações marcou a consolidação do Brasil no mapa de grandes turnês internacionais. Naquele ano, a T4F, produtora responsável pela vinda da cantora, teve uma receita líquida de R$ 700,8 milhões, com 1,09 milhão de ingressos vendidos.

O MorumBIS, que reinou absoluto como a casa tradicional de megashows na capital paulista no início da década passada, viu uma explosão no pós-pandemia. Se antes tinha uma média de três shows por ano, entre 2023 e 2025 foram nove shows por período.

Aproveitando a alta demanda, o estádio do São Paulo assinou um acordo de exclusividade com a produtora Live Nation e virou casa dos maiores shows internacionais do país.

Principais estádios para shows do país, o Nubank Parque tem capacidade para 55 mil pessoas, enquanto o MorumBIS pode receber até 80 mil pessoas.

O g1 pediu entrevistas para representantes da WTorre e das produtoras 30e e LiveNation, que não quiseram responder perguntas sobre a logística de shows.

Nubank adquire naming rights do estádio do Palmeiras — Foto: Divulgação/Nubank

Mas, se o mercado cresceu para todos, o que explica o Nubank Parque sediar um volume muito maior, ultrapassando a marca de 30 grandes apresentações anuais?

Diferente de estádios clássicos, a arena palmeirense já foi concebida para o modelo multiuso . A logística de montagem e desmontagem ganha dias de vantagem graças a acessos projetados para esse fim.

O grande diferencial do estádio palmeirense, no entanto, veio de uma decisão que ocorreu no campo de jogo: a instalação do gramado sintético. Com grama natural, a recuperação do piso após o pisoteio de dezenas de milhares de fãs exige semanas de intervalo. Isso cria uma guerra de calendário entre o futebol e o entretenimento.

O piso artificial eliminou esse gargalo, permitindo uma transição de montagem em tempo bem menor que o comum.

Apesar dos números grandes, a corrida por shows em estádio criou um efeito colateral. Formou-se a ilusão de que todo artista tem público para lotar um estádio.

Um exemplo recente desse descompasso foi o show do Jamiroquai, no estádio do Palmeiras, em setembro. O grupo britânico ficou longe de lotar o espaço.

Mas por que as produtoras insistem em colocar artistas sem apelo de multidão em arenas para 50 mil pessoas? Não valeria realizar mais datas em um espaço menor?

A resposta para essa distorção passa por uma matemática que envolve custos operacionais, logística internacional e a falta de casas de médio porte.

Em primeiro lugar, a experiência adquirida pelas grandes produtoras brasileiras na montagem de megaestruturas barateou significativamente o custo de uma produção única.

Na ponta do lápis, realizar um único show em um estádio mais esvaziado, com 20 ou 30 mil pagantes em uma arena para 50 mil, por exemplo, costuma gerar uma margem de lucro maior do que dividir esse mesmo público em três datas esgotadas numa casa menor. Ao centralizar o evento em um só dia, a produtora paga uma única vez por toda a logística envolvida.

Faixa com o anúncio do show de Bruno Mars no Brasil, pendurada no Estádio Morumbis, em São Paulo — Foto: Live Nation

Além da economia de escala, há o peso do calendário dos estádios e das obrigações contratuais das turnês. A vida de artistas internacionais, por exemplo, está atrelada a turnês pelo continente, com agendas bem apertadas.

Por fim, essa manobra expõe o maior buraco estrutural do mercado brasileiro de entretenimento atual: a falta de casas de médio porte .

As produtoras são forçadas a jogar artistas com fôlego para 15 ou 20 mil ingressos dentro de estádios de futebol porque não há espaços adequados para esse meio-termo. Quando um artista bate no teto de lotação das casas tradicionais "indoor", que costumam comportar, no máximo, cerca de 10 mil pessoas, o próximo degrau já é uma arena gigantesca.

KLB estreiam turnê 20+2 Experience no Vibra São Paulo — Foto: Caio Duran/Opus Entretenimento

Para preencher esse vácuo entre as casas de shows tradicionais e os grandes estádios, os gigantes do setor já começaram a se movimentar. O mercado percebeu que precisa de infraestrutura dedicada e de tamanhos intermediários.

O maior exemplo dessa corrida é a parceria entre a produtora Live Nation e a Cidade Center Norte, que prevê um investimento de R$ 1,5 bilhão na construção de uma arena fechada em São Paulo, com conclusão para 2028 e capacidade para 21 mil pessoas.

A Opus Entretenimento, que administra casas de pequeno porte como a Vibra São Paulo, tem monitorado de perto essa movimentação do mercado e reforça a tese de que o setor carece de palcos que não obriguem o artista a dar um salto cego.

A empresa revelou ao g1 que tem conversas para construção ou administração de novas casas pelo país.

"Os espaços pequenos ou médios não competem com as grandes arenas e estádios, mas atuam de forma complementar. Nem todo artista busca a exposição financeira ou o formato massivo", explica Lucas Zaffari, CEO da Opus.

As arenas de médio porte cumprem um papel estratégico e financeiro fundamental no ecossistema de shows.

O modelo "indoor" já nasce com infraestrutura de ancoragem, estacionamento interno e logística focada 100% em espetáculos, permitindo inclusive residências de várias semanas sem a disputa de datas com o calendário futebolístico.

"Muitos artistas preferem formatos mais flexíveis, para quatro mil pessoas, por exemplo, para que o espaço não pareça vazio. Os estádios foram feitos originalmente para o futebol, enquanto as casas dedicadas oferecem uma conexão muito mais próxima entre o artista e o público", completa Zaffari.

Com a chegada de novos lugares e a valorização dos espaços já existentes, o setor de entretenimento brasileiro passa a oferecer um degrau realista e financeiramente sustentável para as produtoras, corrigindo a rota de um mercado que foi forçado a pensar apenas em megashows.

articles.title: Matthew Perry’s sister recalls ‘Friends’ cast's emotional reunion at funeral;  reveals Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, Matt LeBlanc and David Schwimmer 'stood around him, crying'
articles.summary: Matthew Perry’s sister, Mia Perry Bowick, has shared details about the late actor’s private funeral ceremony.
articles.body: Matthew Perry’s sister, Mia Perry Bowick, has shared details about the late actor’s private funeral ceremony. In his new docu-series, which premiered on Tuesday, October 27, Mia revealed how his five ‘Friends’ co-stars came together to bid an emotional final farewell.The new three-part Netflix documentary, ‘The One About Matthew Perry’, reportedly sees Mia opening up about the private ceremony, which took place at Forest Lawn Memorial Park in Los Angeles in November 2023. She said Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, Matt LeBlanc and David Schwimmer arrived together to pay their final respects. “I hadn’t seen them in easily 20 years,” she said, via People.Mia then went on to reveal that Jennifer was the first to approach her and offer a hug, before the other cast members followed. She then recalled a particularly moving moment as the five actors gathered around Matthew’s casket. “And then, all five of them walked up to the casket holding hands and stood around him, crying,” she recalled.The funeral was a private gathering attended by Matthew’s family and closest friends, held six days after his death. Following the news of his passing, the five surviving ‘Friends’ stars had released a joint statement expressing their devastation at losing someone they considered family. The statement read, “We are all so utterly devastated by the loss of Matthew. We were more than just castmates. We are a family. There is so much to say, but right now we’re going to take a moment to grieve and process this unfathomable loss. In time we will say more, as and when we are able. For now, our thoughts and our love are with Matty’s family, his friends, and everyone who loved him around the world.”The documentary arrived a day before the third anniversary of Matthew’s death on October 28, 2023. The actor, best known for his performance as Chandler Bing, was 54 at the time of his demise.According to reports, while the 'Friends' cast is mentioned in the series, and features in archival footage, none of them took part in fresh interviews for the project.Director Mary Robertson ‘The One About Matthew Perry’ explores the actor’s life and career, his struggles with addiction, and the memories shared by those who knew him best.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Ah! Leah!' and 'Love Is Like a Rock' singer Donnie Iris passes away at age 83
articles.summary: Music legend Donnie Iris, known for hits like 'Ah! Leah!' and 'Love Is Like a Rock,' has passed away at 83 after a brave fight against bladder cancer. His legacy and influence on Pittsburgh's music scene will be remembered.
articles.body: Beloved singer Donnie Iris has passed away at 83 after battling bladder cancer for the past three years. He was best known for his work with The Jaggerz, Wild Cherry, and Donnie Iris and the Cruisers. His family and friends shared the news of the iconic singer-songwriter’s passing in an official statement to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. The statement announcing the tragic news left everyone grieving and in shock.Donnie Iris passes away at 83Iris' colleague, Joe Grushecky, remembered the legendary musician and shared, "For my money, he was the most beloved Pittsburgh musician of all time. I don't know anyone who was loved more than Donnie. He just had that warmth about him, and it came through in his performance."In another statement from longtime keyboard player and best friend Mark Avsec, he fondly remembered Iris and shared with the outlet, "He sang like a bird that night. It was the first time on a chair, and he didn’t like that. But the poor guy, the cancer was spreading, and he was in pain, and he really wanted to do that show and be with the people.”Who was Donnie Iris?Born in Pittsburgh in 1943, Donnie Iris was a legendary musician. He established his connection with music very early in life. He first started singing and performing in a doo-wop group in high school during the early ’60s. He then moved on to rock ‘n’ roll and R&B cover bands before The Jaggerz were finally formed in 1964 and released their debut album in 1969, titled ‘Introducing the Jaggerz.'In the 70s, Wild Cherry had already established themselves in the music scene; however, Iris joined the group and released multiple songs. While working with this group, he found his best friend, Avsec, who followed him when Donnie started the group Donnie Iris and the Cruisers. The two had just shared the stage last month.Donnie Iris played his final performance on September 28, 2026, at the grand opening of Citizens Live at The Wylie in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. articles.title: Taylor Swift’s hitmaker scolds Ed Sheeran, ‘stand the f--- up’ after Macklemore fallout
articles.summary: Jack Antonoff said Ed Sheeran missed a "massive" chance to defy billionaire pressure after removing Macklemore from his Loop Tour over Palestine remarks.
articles.body: Grammy-winning producer Jack Antonoff said Ed Sheeran missed a "massive" opportunity to "stand the f--- up" to billionaire interests, criticizing the English singer for removing Macklemore from his tour over the rapper’s remarks on Israel-Palestinian conflict. Antonoff, lead singer for the band Bleachers and producer behind some of Taylor Swift’s biggest hits, made the scathing rebuke in a recent interview with The Guardian, more than a month after Sheeran faced backlash over Macklemore’s removal from the Loop Tour following the rapper’s calls for "Free Palestine" during his opening act. "If you think it is [controversial] you’re lost in some other sauce that is so crazy. They’re going to let some f---ing promoter tell me what I can say? Don’t book me. I’ll play for free outside," Antonoff told the outlet. COLIN KAEPERNICK ACCUSES NFL OF 'COLLUDING' AGAINST MACKLEMORE AMID 'FREE PALESTINE' CONTROVERSY New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was among a group of NFL team owners who reportedly threatened to bar Sheeran’s stadium performances if Macklemore was included in the lineup. Antonoff argued that Sheeran should have canceled the tour and staged free concerts outside the venues rather than give in to pressure from billionaires. "[Ed Sheeran] missed a massive, beautiful opportunity there: just cancel the whole f---ing tour, then play for free outside each venue, raise a bunch of money, rather than let a f---ing billionaire tell you what to do," Antonoff said. "The reason it’s not an anomaly or niche issue is because we all live in a world where billionaires are constantly telling us what to do. So stand the f--- up." KATHY GRIFFIN SAYS ED SHEERAN SHOULD HAVE TOLD ROBERT KRAFT TO 'GO F--- YOURSELF' OVER MACKLEMORE Sheeran addressed the controversy during his Philadelphia tour stop, saying in part: "What happened in Israel and at the Nova Music Festival on Oct. 7 was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate." Several other artists scheduled to open for Sheeran, including Finneas, Aaron Rowe and Lukas Graham, dropped out of the tour in solidarity with Macklemore, who has doubled down on his message with a "Free Palestine Tour." Antonoff, who has also voiced support for a "free Palestine," praised Macklemore for speaking out. The Jewish artist said he has "felt way more emboldened to say it now." "It’s not in any way a strange, uncomfortable or controversial thing to say, it’s a deeply human thing to say," said the producer. ED SHEERAN APOLOGIZES FOR MACKLEMORE BACKLASH, ENCOURAGES UNITY AT FIRST CONCERT SINCE FALLOUT Film critic and Hollywood in Toto founder and editor Christian Toto told Fox News Digital that Antonoff does not care about free speech, arguing that his comments are an attempt to gain approval within his industry. "Jack doesn't sound well-informed, either about Middle East politics or his own business," Toto said in a statement. "If Sheeran scrapped his tour, how many workers would lose their jobs? And, if he did an alternative tour, how would they get paid?" "He knows it's acceptable within his industry to blanketly bash billionaires, a lazy, thoughtless attack and do a variation of ‘Free Palestine,'" Toto continued. "He's trying to curry favor within his industry. Sadly, it might just work." articles.title: Newcastle to host 2027 6 Music Festival
articles.summary: The station's flagship festival will return to Tyneside after 12 years.
articles.body:
BBC Radio 6 Music has announced the 2027 edition of its annual festival will take place in Newcastle.

After four years in Greater Manchester, the festival will take place across Newcastle's independent and grassroots venues in March with five days of performances and DJ sets.

Tyneside last hosted the festival in 2015 but principal advisor for events and culture at Newcastle City Council, Jim Mawdsley, said since then "Newcastle has become a true music city".

Head of BBC Radio 6 Music Samantha Moy said: "The city and the region have such a rich musical legacy and a thriving creative community, which will make for another wonderful setting."

Newcastle has enjoyed recent success with national music events, having just hosted the Mercury Prize for the second year in a row.

The city also hosted the MOBO Awards in 2025.

The 6 Music Festival has been running since 2014 and initially was a roving event, moving around the country each year before settling in Manchester in 2023.

6 Music presenter Lauren Laverne said: "Having grown up in the North East, I know just how much music means to people here and the important role it plays in local culture and communities.

"It's fantastic to see the festival return to the North East, and I can't wait to join listeners, artists and presenters for what promises to be a brilliant celebration of live music."

In 2026, the festival saw performances from the likes of Bloc Party, Courtney Barnett and Jacob Alon.

Mawdsley said: "Since it was last here, Newcastle has become a true music city with many of our artists being recognised not least by awards like the Mercury Prize, which has shortlisted Sam Fender, Jade and Knats in the last two years, but there is a real collaborative spirit in the city.

"Music is a vital element of our cultural lifeblood, and we can't wait to welcome 6 Music listeners to learn more about how vibrant the city has become."

6 Music Festival 2027 will take place 15-19 March and the full lineup and venues will be announced next year.

articles.body: The first reactions to Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' are emerging, following the film’s premiere in Los Angeles on Tuesday night. In his initial, spoiler-free reaction, the reviewer praised the film, while comparing the experience to watching ‘The Lord of the Rings’ for the first time.Taking to his social media handle shortly after the screening, he posted a video saying, "I really don't know how to even start this out of the theatre reaction. There is nothing out there in the cinematic universe like what I just watched. And people can take that in a good way or a negative way. There's just nothing like it."‘Ramayana’ compared to ‘The Lord of the Rings’Explaining what he had hoped to experience from the film, he said, "I wanted a great story, and I wanted, like, something that, like... told me something, and taught me something, and everyone keeps telling me that Ramayana is, you know, true history, and it's the Indian culture, and it means a lot to them. I haven't felt like this since, like, the very first time, in 2001, since, the first 'Lord of the Rings' movie. Like, this movie is very grand. It's very epic."Ranbir Kapoor hailed for turn as Lord RamaThe reviewer also singled out the character of Rama, expressing surprise at the portrayal. With the second instalment reportedly scheduled for release on Diwali 2027, the reviewer said, "I can't give away spoilers, but the cliffhanger... when that movie ended, when the screen went black, I literally said, no, like, I shouted out loud, no."Hindi version confirmed to have longer runtimeThe reviewer also highlighted the film's runtime and explained why he chose to watch the original Hindi version rather than an English-dubbed cut. He said, "Listen, this is a big, weighty movie. It's over 3 hours. I watched the original Hindi version. I didn't had no interest in watching the English dubbed version that was cut by 30 minutes. I wanted to see the authentic movie. I wanted to see this movie."Summing up his experience, he concluded, "I mean, I felt, I feel like, I know this is true story and true history. I felt like I just left a fairy tale. It's the best way I can describe this film now..."'Ramayana' gets mixed feedbackThe post featured a rather mixed reaction, stating, "The ambition and scale deserve a lot of applause. articles.title: ‘Gondhal’ director Santosh Davakhar on India’s Oscar entry, Diwali release in 7 languages and more: ''Ramayana' would give our film more room' - Exclusive
articles.summary: Marathi cinema is increasingly finding its place in the national conversation, but taking regional stories to a wider audience comes with its own set of
articles.body: Marathi cinema is increasingly finding its place in the national conversation, but taking regional stories to a wider audience comes with its own set of challenges. Director Santosh Davakhar hopes to bridge that gap with ‘Gondhal’, a psychological thriller rooted in Maharashtra’s cultural traditions that blends devotion, deception, desire and betrayal. Selected as India’s official entry for the 99th Academy Awards, the film is set for a worldwide release in seven languages on November 13, following the arrival of ‘Ramayana’ on November 5.For Davakhar, the film represents an opportunity to introduce Maharashtra’s cultural heritage to audiences beyond the Marathi-speaking world while demonstrating the universal appeal of stories rooted in regional identities. From retaining the authenticity of a traditional ritual across multiple language versions to navigating marketing challenges, theatrical distribution and the struggle for screens, the filmmaker believes that strong storytelling and audience support are essential for Marathi cinema to grow.The director also opens up about the responsibility of representing India on the international stage, why he believes ‘Gondhal’ deserves to be experienced in theatres, and how the Oscar campaign has temporarily put his next project, ‘Shahaji Raje’, on hold. In this conversation, Davakhar shares his vision for the future of Marathi cinema, including his ambitious dream of seeing the industry achieve ₹1,000 crore in annual box-office collections within the next five years.‘Gondhal’ is releasing worldwide in seven languages on November 13, shortly after ‘Ramayana’ on November 5. How significant is this release window, and does the pan-India ambition bring added expectations?We originally wanted a Diwali release. With ‘Ramayana’ arriving on November 5 and the excitement surrounding it, we felt November 13 would give our film more room. By the following week, audiences may be ready for a different experience. Releasing worldwide in seven languages is a big step for us. It brings expectations, but also the hope that our Marathi story will connect with a much wider audience. Their support can strengthen our Oscar campaign too.The film’s trailer has now been released globally. What was the central thought behind the story, and what do you hope audiences take away from it?From the beginning, I wanted to tell a story rooted in Maharashtra that could represent India internationally. I spoke about that dream even a year before the film’s release. ‘Gondhal’ brings together devotion, deception, desire and betrayal. A sacred ritual becomes the setting for a psychological thriller. I want audiences to feel the suspense and leave thinking about the characters, their choices and the consequences.Taking a Marathi film to audiences across seven languages is a big step. How challenging was it to retain its cultural authenticity while making it accessible to viewers from different regions?The challenge was to make the dialogue feel natural in every language while preserving Marathi culture, traditional music and the village atmosphere. At its heart, the film explores complex human emotions such as jealousy, greed, the struggle for power and obsession. These emotions connect with people everywhere. Audiences may be unfamiliar with the ritual, but they will understand the characters and what drives them.With ‘Gondhal’ drawing attention as India’s official entry for the 99th Academy Awards, how has that recognition influenced your approach to presenting it internationally?Being India’s official entry makes international audiences take notice, but it also brings responsibility. India is a diverse country, with rich traditions in every corner. Through ‘Gondhal’, we are trying to preserve and share one of those traditions. We want international audiences to discover this culture through its people and their story. Representing our culture, our community and our country together is a huge honour and a dream come true.What sets ‘Gondhal’ apart from other films releasing around the same time, and why should audiences experience it in theatres?‘Gondhal’ is completely a team effort. Every head of department and every team member has contributed to its quality. The FFI jury told us they chose the film because it was the best across departments, including acting. That appreciation belongs to the whole team. Some of our actors may not be famous faces, but they deliver powerful performances.The 25-minute opening take, unpredictable twists, visuals and live sound draw you into a remote village in Maharashtra and make you feel part of its world. Please watch it in theatres. That is where you can fully experience everyone’s work together. We created it for the big screen, and we are not currently planning an OTT release.How important is marketing for a Marathi film today, especially when competing with big-budget Hindi and South Indian releases?Marketing is essential because even a good film needs to reach people. We are a small production house, so we must use our resources carefully while putting quality first. Today’s audiences know what they want: a strong story and a fresh experience. Our marketing must make them curious enough to buy a ticket. After that, the film must earn their appreciation. Word of mouth can become our strongest support.Could your next film also be rooted in Marathi culture, or are you looking to tell a story with a more pan-India setting?My next film, ‘Shahaji Raje’, is rooted in Maharashtra’s history and pride. The screenplay and dialogues are ready, and we were preparing to begin shooting. We have now put it on hold for three to four months to give ‘Gondhal’ and its Oscar campaign our complete attention. India has given us a big responsibility, and we want to give it our best. I believe a story rooted in Maharashtra can still connect with audiences across the country.What is one change you would like to see in the Marathi film industry over the next five years?I would love to see a stronger bond between Marathi films and their audiences. It must be a two-way effort: filmmakers need to create fresh, engaging stories, and audiences need to support them in theatres. My dream is that, within the next five years, Marathi cinema reaches ₹1,000 crore in annual box-office collections. That growth would create opportunities for new talent, more stories and ambitious films.A Marathi film can win awards and represent India at the Oscars, but can it get enough screens at home? How do you respond to that contradiction?It is a real concern. International recognition does not automatically bring enough screens or suitable showtimes at home. But our limited Hindi paid previews received an encouraging response. At our Pune screening, even tourists took time out of their visit to watch the film and came away happy. That gives me confidence.Kannada cinema faced similar challenges before a few major successes helped it reach audiences across India. I believe Marathi cinema can do the same. This year, ‘Krantijyoti Vidyalay Marathi Madhyam’, ‘Deool Band 2’ and ‘Raja Shivaji’ together have done around ₹250 crore in worldwide business. Their success shows the strength of stories rooted in our culture. We need to build on that momentum and give more Marathi films a fair chance to reach their audiences.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
