articles.title: Halloween watchlist: 20  films from the 21st century that reshaped horror
articles.body: 1. Don’t Breathe (2016)Director: Fede ÁlvarezThree young burglars break into the home of a war veteran, believing that his isolation makes him an easy target. Rocky hopes to use the stolen money to escape her abusive home, while her companions see the robbery as a quick financial opportunity. Their plan collapses…Fede Álvarez builds suspense through precise spatial choreography and carefully controlled silence. Although the increasingly extreme twists occasionally strain credibility, the film remains an effective examination of desperation, moral compromise and the dangers of underestimating someone because they appear vulnerable.2. Goodnight Mommy (2014)Directors: Veronika Franz and Severin FialaTwin brothers Elias and Lukas return home to find their mother recovering from facial surgery, her head covered in bandages. Expecting affection and familiarity, they instead encounter a woman who behaves coldly, imposes strict rules and seems emotionally distant. Gradually, the boys become convinced that she is an impostor who has replaced their real mother.Ordinary disagreements become increasingly disturbing as the twins subject the woman to cruel tests intended to establish her identity. The directors encourage viewers to share the children's uncertainty, making it difficult to distinguish genuine evidence from the products of fear and imagination.3. Good Boy (2025)Director: Ben LeonbergTold largely from the perspective of a dog named Indy, Good Boy follows his attempts to protect his human companion, Todd, after they move into a secluded family home. Todd's health is deteriorating, and the property appears to harbour a disturbing supernatural presence. Indy senses danger in empty rooms, unfamiliar shadows and strange sounds that the humans cannot fully understand.The film’s unusual perspective creates suspense without relying on conventional dialogue or exposition. Indy cannot explain what he sees, so his fear emerges through barking, body language, hesitation and his determination to remain near Todd. The audience is left to interpret the threat through the same limited information available to the animal.4. A Quiet Place (2018)Director: John KrasinskiIn a devastated America, a family struggles to survive among blind creatures that hunt through sound. Lee and Evelyn Abbott and their children communicate through sign language, walk carefully along prepared paths and suppress every avoidable noise. Their elaborate precautions reflect a world where even a small mistake can prove fatal.John Krasinski transforms silence into the film's central dramatic device. Footsteps, creaking floorboards and unexpected noises acquire extraordinary significance. The monsters provide the external threat, but the emotional story concerns parental responsibility, grief and the difficulties of protecting children without being able to control every danger.5. Get Out (2017)Director: Jordan PeeleChris Washington, a photographer, accompanies his girlfriend, Rose, to meet her parents at their country estate. Their apparently progressive hospitality soon becomes unsettling, particularly when the household’s Black employees behave strangely and the family's wealthy guests display an uncomfortable fascination with Chris's body and physical abilities. Jordan Peele gradually transforms social awkwardness into psychological horror.6. Knock at the Cabin (2023)Director: M. Night ShyamalanEric and Andrew are vacationing with their young daughter, Wen, when four strangers arrive at their secluded cabin. Led by Leonard, the visitors insist that the family must make an unbearable choice: one of the two men must willingly die to prevent an impending apocalypse.Shyamalan confines much of the action to the cabin, allowing the characters' limited knowledge to generate tension. Dave Bautista is particularly effective as Leonard, whose imposing physical presence contrasts with his apparent gentleness and anguish. The film's central dilemma is about the limits of moral responsibility: should people sacrifice someone they love for the survival of strangers, especially when certainty is impossible?7. Ginger Snaps (2000)Director: John FawcettGinger and Brigitte Fitzgerald are teenage sisters who feel alienated from their suburban surroundings and share a fascination with death. Their intense bond begins to fracture when Ginger is attacked by a mysterious creature during her first menstruation. She survives, but her body and personality begin changing in disturbing ways.Ginger becomes more assertive and sexually confident, attracting attention from boys while growing increasingly aggressive. The werewolf mythology gives physical form to anxieties about menstruation, sexuality and female adolescence. Ginger's transformation is both empowering and destructive, while Brigitte faces the painful possibility of losing the person whose identity has always been intertwined with her own.8. A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night (2014)Director: Ana Lily AmirpourSet in the fictional Iranian town of Bad City, this black-and-white film follows a nameless young woman who wanders the streets at night. She is a vampire who preys on men whose behaviour is exploitative or abusive, becoming an unsettling presence in a community marked by addiction, prostitution and neglect.Her life intersects with that of Arash, a young man struggling to care for his drug-addicted father. Their growing connection develops through shared loneliness rather than conventional romantic gestures. Both characters inhabit a world where intimacy is difficult and survival demands moral compromises.9. Cloverfield (2008)Director: Matt ReevesPresented as recovered camcorder footage, Cloverfield follows a group of young New Yorkers caught in a sudden monster attack. The disaster interrupts a farewell party for Rob Hawkins, whose personal problems initially seem far more important than the unexplained explosions shaking the city.As Manhattan descends into chaos, the group discovers that a gigantic creature is attacking buildings and destroying streets. The found-footage format restricts the audience to what the characters can see and understand. The shaky camera, fragmented information and sudden changes in direction recreate the confusion of civilians experiencing a disaster without knowing its cause.10. I Saw the Devil (2010)Director: Kim Jee-woonWhen his pregnant fiancée is murdered by serial killer Jang Kyung-chul, intelligence agent Kim Soo-hyun embarks on a personal campaign of revenge. The pursuit becomes an increasingly disturbing contest between two men whose actions draw them towards the same moral darkness. This movie is an uncompromising psychological thriller about grief, obsession and the corruption of moral purpose.11. The Host (2006)Director: Bong Joon HoA monstrous creature emerges from Seoul's Han River after toxic chemicals are improperly disposed of in a laboratory. During an attack on the riverbank, it abducts Hyun-seo, the young daughter of Park Gang-du, who runs a snack kiosk nearby. Her family is devastated, but their attempts to rescue her are complicated by authorities who impose quarantine and insist that the creature carries a dangerous virus.Bong combines creature horror with dark comedy and social satire, linking the disaster to environmental negligence and institutional failure. The monster is frighteningly physical, but the film's emotional centre remains the family's refusal to abandon a missing child.12. Crimson Peak (2015)Director: Guillermo del ToroEdith Cushing, an aspiring writer fascinated by ghost stories, falls in love with Thomas Sharpe, an English aristocrat seeking financial support for an invention. Despite her father's reservations, she marries Thomas and moves to his ancestral mansion, Allerdale Hall, a decaying Gothic structure that appears to be sinking into the surrounding red clay.Living there with Thomas and his possessive sister Lucille, Edith begins experiencing disturbing supernatural manifestations. Guillermo del Toro builds the film around the visual traditions of Gothic romance. Elaborate costumes, stark colours and grotesque supernatural imagery make the mansion an essential part of the storytelling. Crimson Peak explores the disturbing possibility that the people who claim to love us may also be the ones most capable of destroying us.13. The Orphanage (2007)Director: J. A. BayonaLaura returns to the former orphanage where she grew up, intending to reopen it as a home for children with special needs. She arrives with her husband, Carlos, and their adopted son, Simón, whose mysterious imaginary companions begin to unsettle the household.During a gathering at the property, Simón disappears. Laura launches a desperate search, convinced that the old building contains clues to his whereabouts. As the police investigation fails to provide answers, she becomes increasingly absorbed in the orphanage's history and the possibility that the children who once lived there have left behind a supernatural presence.Bayona uses the house's corridors, locked rooms and concealed spaces to build suspense without relying excessively on graphic violence. The mystery gradually becomes inseparable from Laura's grief and determination to find her son.14. Annihilation (2018)Director: Alex GarlandBiologist Lena joins an expedition into the Shimmer, an expanding and unexplained phenomenon surrounding an isolated coastal region. Her husband, Kane, has returned from an earlier mission physically deteriorating and unable to explain what happened inside. Determined to understand his condition, Lena enters the affected zone with a team of scientists.Within the Shimmer, the natural world behaves in increasingly disturbing ways. Plants grow in human-like forms, animals mutate and familiar biological boundaries dissolve as DNA appears to be rearranged. The expedition members also experience psychological disturbances, making it difficult to separate external threats from their own vulnerabilities.Garland combines science-fiction spectacle with cosmic horror, creating an environment that resists ordinary explanation. The Shimmer also functions as a metaphor for self-destruction, grief and the human desire to escape painful aspects of existence.15. The Descent (2005)Director: Neil MarshallA year after losing her husband and daughter in an accident, Sarah joins five female friends on a caving expedition. The trip is intended to help her reconnect with them, but the adventure turns disastrous when a collapse blocks their route out of an unexplored cave system.Their predicament becomes far worse when they encounter subterranean humanoid creatures adapted to life in darkness. The group must improvise weapons, conserve supplies and search for an escape route while being hunted underground.The monsters are not the only source of danger. Secrets and betrayals within the group intensify existing tensions, while Sarah's grief gradually gives way to a more aggressive determination to survive. The Descent is a ferocious survival horror film in which physical terror and psychological collapse reinforce each other.16. Shaun of the Dead (2004)Director: Edgar WrightShaun is an underachieving electronics salesman whose life revolves around his best friend Ed, their local pub and a deteriorating relationship with his girlfriend Liz. When Liz leaves him, Shaun is forced to confront his lack of direction. At the same time, a zombie outbreak begins spreading through London.Edgar Wright combines horror conventions with tightly edited visual comedy and affectionate references to classic zombie cinema. The undead also function as a satire of everyday inertia, their repetitive movements reflecting the routines that have trapped Shaun in an unsatisfying life. Beneath the comedy lies a coming-of-age story about responsibility and friendship.17. The Witch (2015)Director: Robert EggersIn seventeenth-century New England, a deeply religious family is expelled from its Puritan settlement and establishes an isolated farm beside a vast forest. William, his wife Katherine and their children believe that strict faith and hard work will protect them, but their fragile existence collapses when their youngest child disappears while under the care of his older sister, Thomasin.The family begins suspecting witchcraft as further disturbing events unfold.Eggers recreates the period through archaic dialogue, historical detail and a restrained visual style. The horror emerges from the collision between religious certainty and a reality that refuses easy explanation.18. The Conjuring (2013)Director: James WanThe Perron family moves into an isolated Rhode Island farmhouse during the 1970s, hoping for a fresh start. Strange events soon disrupt their lives: clocks stop, unexplained noises echo through the house, objects move. The disturbances gradually become more violent, particularly for Carolyn Perron and her five daughters.Desperate for help, Carolyn contacts paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren. Wan builds suspense through careful sound design, dark corridors and concealed spaces. Rather than immediately revealing every supernatural presence, he encourages viewers to anticipate danger in the edges of the frame.The story's central conflict is ultimately about protection. Carolyn's determination to save her children drives the narrative, while Ed and Lorraine's partnership provides a counterpoint to the fear surrounding them.19. Let the Right One In (2008)Director: Tomas AlfredsonOskar is a lonely twelve-year-old boy living in a bleak Stockholm suburb, where he endures persistent bullying at school. His life changes when Eli, an unusual girl, moves into the neighbouring apartment with an older man. Although Eli initially insists that they cannot be friends, the two children gradually develop a bond built on their shared isolation.As mysterious killings disturb the neighbourhood, Oskar discovers something chilling. Alfredson uses snow-covered courtyards, dimly lit apartments and sparse dialogue to create an atmosphere of profound melancholy. The horror is often graphic, but the film's central concern is emotional rather than sensational.20. 28 Days Later (2002)Director: Danny BoyleJim, a bicycle courier, awakens from a coma to discover that London has been abandoned following a devastating viral outbreak. The infection, known as Rage, spreads through bodily fluids and transforms its victims into violently aggressive carriers. Unlike traditional slow-moving zombies, the infected sprint towards their prey, making every encounter immediate and terrifying.Jim joins survivors Selena, Frank and Frank's daughter Hannah as they attempt to reach a reported military refuge.Danny Boyle’s grainy digital cinematography gives the empty city a haunting immediacy, while rapid editing intensifies the infected attacks.28 Days Later helped reinvent modern zombie cinema by combining fast-moving infected, urban desolation and a bleak examination of how catastrophe exposes both human cruelty and the need for connection.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Jailer 2' box office collection Day 14 [LIVE]: Rajinikanth’s action drama crosses Rs 416 crore India net, nears Rs 490 crore gross
articles.summary: Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2' is continuing its theatrical run as the action entertainer enters its 14th day at the box office.
articles.body: Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2' is continuing its theatrical run as the action entertainer enters its 14th day at the box office. The Nelson Dilipkumar directorial has crossed Rs 416 crore in India net collections, while its domestic gross earnings are nearing the Rs 490 crore mark. After a strong opening week and a steady second-week performance, the film is now adding to its total through Tamil, Telugu and Hindi screenings. The latest live figures offer an early look at its weekday performance, with the final numbers for Wednesday yet to be reported.‘Jailer 2’ India box office collection surpasses Rs 416 crore netAccording to Sacnilk, 'Jailer 2' has collected Rs 1.13 crore net in India on Day 14 so far. The film opened with Rs 59.70 crore on its first day and reportedly earned Rs 334.35 crore net during its opening week. It continued to draw audiences in the following days, although weekday collections have shown signs of a slowdown. The latest update takes its India net total to Rs 416.78 crore, while its domestic gross collection stands at Rs 487.83 crore. The final Day 14 collection is yet to be reported, and the figures may change as more shows are tracked.‘Jailer 2’ Day 14 Live box office collectionAs of Day 14, 'Jailer 2' is running across 3,946 tracked shows in India. The Tamil version remains the biggest contributor, collecting Rs 0.89 crore from 1,827 shows. The Telugu version has added Rs 0.53 crore through 779 shows, while the Hindi version has earned Rs 0.21 crore from 1,340 shows. Together, the three language versions have contributed Rs 1.63 crore in live India net earnings.The Tamil version continues to lead the film’s language-wise collections, accounting for the largest share of its latest daily total.‘Jailer 2’ day-wise box office collectionWeek 1: Rs 334.35 croreDay 8: Rs 17.15 croreDay 9: Rs 14.50 croreDay 10: Rs 24.15 croreDay 11: Rs 25.70 croreDay 12: Rs 9.45 croreDay 13: Rs 7.50 croreDay 14 [LIVE]: Rs 1.63 croreTotal India net: Rs 417.28 croreEyes on Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’ third week box officeDirected by Nelson Dilipkumar, ‘Jailer 2’ features Rajinikanth as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, with Mohanlal, Shivarajkumar, Ramya Krishnan, Vidya Balan, Jackie Shroff, Mithun Chakraborty, S. J. Suryah and Yogi Babu in key roles. Anirudh Ravichander has composed the music for the sequel. With the film’s worldwide gross previously reported at Rs 744 crore, attention remains on whether it can move closer to the Rs 1,000 crore milestone.
